subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should OpenClaw expose session archive/rotation as a durable automation event, and should the supported boundary be core cron schedule syntax, a plugin SDK lifecycle/API seam, or a plugin-owned workflow?
rationale: The missing source capability is clear, but the permanent shape affects cron config, plugin API stability, sensitive session metadata, and silent agent-turn execution policy, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Design a durable lifecycle event contract
options.body: Approve a scoped `session_end`/archive event model with event id, minimal metadata, permission/audit rules, and cron/plugin dispatch semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep lifecycle handling plugin-only
options.body: Treat existing `session_end` hooks as the supported boundary and ask plugin authors to implement automation outside cron until a concrete missing SDK operation is specified.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub package design
options.body: Ask for this as a ClawHub plugin or bundle first, then add only the narrow core/plugin API that package proves is missing.

recommendation.title: Design a durable lifecycle event contract
recommendation.body: Approve a scoped `session_end`/archive event model with event id, minimal metadata, permission/audit rules, and cron/plugin dispatch semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is tied to the cron foundation and is the best available owner for the cross-cutting cron/session/product boundary decision.
